newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy GDP will not meet govt targets - Confindustria.
newsitem.headline: Italy GDP will not meet govt targets - Confindustria.

text.p: Italy's economy will pick up in the second half of the year, but average gross domestic product (GDP) will not grow by more than one percent in 1997 as a whole, Italian industrialists group Confindustria said in a report.
The economic survey predicted GDP growth of 1.8 percent in 1998 and 2.3 percent in 1999.
By contract, Italy's centre-left government has forecast economic growth of 1.2 percent this year, 2.0 percent in 1998 and 2.5 percent in 1999.

"The signs of a recovery in output that we saw in the first months of 1997 will be confirmed in the second half, but GDP growth will not exceed an average one percent this year and will stay below its potential in 1998," the report said.
Italian GDP fell by 0.5 percent year-on-year, in the first quarter of 1997, but industrial output has shown signs of picking up, climbing an adjusted 0.7 percent month-on-month in April.
Confindustria said it was surprised how low inflation had fallen in April and May. "But (it) should increase by a few decimal points in the coming months," the report said.
"This will not prevent an average inflation figure of around 2.1 percent (in 1997), well below the official target, but could put at risk the...1998 target," it added.

The government has forecast average inflation of 1.8 percent next year. Confindustria said there needed to be changes to the way wage settlements were worked out to be sure of hitting the 1998 target.

For 1997, the government originally forecast an average rate of 2.5 percent, but Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said at the weekend he expected average inflation of under two percent this year.
Preliminary data from 10 Italian cities pointed to an inflation rate of 1.4 percent year-on-year in June. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
